name: Bristol
intro: From Victorian terraces in the north to Georgian townhouses on the hill, we have planned projects in nearly every corner of the city since 2009.
homes: Victorian terraces, Edwardian semis and Georgian townhouses
focus: Kitchen extensions, loft conversions and whole-house renovations
note: Planning and conservation rules vary across the city. We will tell you early which apply to your street.
project: Kitchen and rear extension, Bishopston terrace

name: Bath
intro: Bath stone, listed facades and World Heritage expectations. Projects here reward patience and the right specialists.
homes: Listed Georgian terraces, Bath stone villas and mews cottages
focus: Sympathetic restorations, basement conversions and garden rooms
note: Much of the city is a conservation area, and many homes are listed. We plan listed building consent into the timeline from day one.

name: Clifton
intro: Tall ceilings, deep cornicing and awkward upper floors. Clifton homes are generous, but rarely straightforward.
homes: Georgian and Regency townhouses, often divided into flats
focus: Flat reconfigurations, sash window repair and lower-ground kitchens
note: Clifton is a conservation area with an Article 4 direction on many streets. External changes need careful handling.

name: Redland
intro: Big Victorian semis with gardens that ask for a proper kitchen. Redland is where we see some of our most ambitious extensions.
homes: Large Victorian semis and red-brick villas
focus: Side-return and wraparound extensions, loft suites
note: Party wall agreements are common on semis here, and we build them into the plan from the start.

name: Bishopston
intro: Gloucester Road neighbours, narrow side returns and families who have outgrown the back room. We know these terraces by heart.
homes: Two-up two-down and bay-fronted Victorian terraces
focus: Side-return kitchens, dormer lofts and bathroom moves
note: Most rear dormers here fall under permitted development, but we check every street before you spend a penny on drawings.
project: Kitchen and rear extension, Bishopston terrace

name: Southville
intro: Colourful terraces, small gardens and clever use of every square metre. Southville projects are about making space feel bigger.
homes: Compact Victorian terraces and former workers' cottages
focus: Open-plan ground floors, compact lofts and garden studios
note: Some streets sit close to the floodplain. We flag drainage and damp considerations before any design work begins.

name: Bedminster
intro: North Street energy and a growing number of first homes ready for their first proper renovation.
focus: First-home renovations, rewires and kitchen refits
note: Older terraces here often need rewiring and replastering. We price those honestly so the budget does not unravel later.

name: Westbury-on-Trym
intro: Interwar detached homes and village-feel streets, with room to grow outwards and upwards.
focus: Two-storey extensions, garage conversions and energy upgrades
note: Larger extensions here usually need full planning permission. We help you brief the right architect at the right moment.

name: Henleaze
intro: Solid family homes, mature gardens and owners who want to stay put for the long run.
homes: Edwardian and interwar semis with long gardens
focus: Kitchen-diner extensions, loft conversions and insulation
note: Many homes here suit a heat pump upgrade. We can fold energy improvements into the same project plan.

name: Fishponds
intro: Good-sized terraces and semis with real potential, often at the start of a longer renovation story.
homes: Victorian and Edwardian terraces, post-war semis
focus: Phased renovations, rear extensions and bathroom refits
note: We often plan Fishponds projects in phases, so the work can follow the budget rather than the other way round.

name: Portishead
intro: Marina townhouses, older seafront homes and plenty of newer builds ready to be made personal.
homes: Modern townhouses, Victorian seafront villas and 1970s detached houses
focus: Kitchen remodels, garden rooms and layout changes in newer builds
note: Newer homes may carry covenants or management rules. We check the paperwork before you commit to a design.

name: Keynsham
intro: Between Bristol and Bath, with homes that range from stone cottages to generous post-war semis.
homes: Stone cottages, post-war semis and modern family homes
focus: Single-storey extensions, loft conversions and garage conversions
note: Keynsham falls under Bath and North East Somerset Council, so planning timings differ from Bristol. We plan for that.
